last_green_commit_note: Exact §1 builder candidate. Codex Critic independently re-ran the full tests and production build against this executable source; the critic commit changes review/state documentation only.

tests.summary: Codex Critic independently re-ran the suite: 51 test files passed; 278 of 278 tests passed (was 46 files / 239 tests at §0).

build.summary: Codex Critic independently re-ran the Next.js 16.2.11 production build: compilation and TypeScript passed; 16 static-page tasks generated.
build.font_network_behavior: Unchanged from §0: src/app/layout.tsx still imports Inter, JetBrains Mono, and Instrument Serif from next/font/google. Not silently absorbed into §1 — remains §13 work.

visual.note: Critic inspection found that the shell public file labeled 1440x900 is 892x779; the other desktop files labeled 1440x900 are 991x865; the committed mobile files are 614x667. Genuine required target screenshots are absent.
visual.critic_live_check: The final CSS shell was independently rendered at true 1440x900, 390x844, and 320x844. Both phone widths matched document/client width with no horizontal overflow; five chapter targets were exactly 44px tall.
visual.mobile_capture_limitation: This session's browser automation could not resize below ~614 CSS px (vs. the required 390/320 targets). The 614px capture exercises the same max-width:767px rule 390/320 would hit — see docs/phase10-baseline/section-1/README.md 'Mobile capture limitation' for the full explanation and mitigations (forced-fallback screenshots + a CSS-source invariant test). No 390px/320px screenshot is claimed.

accessibility.chapter_navigation: ObservatoryShell/ChapterOrbit now provide real five-chapter semantic navigation (one <nav>, one real link per chapter, aria-current on the active one) with a working static/no-3D fallback — the §0 gap this section exists to close. Not yet wired into /share, /, or /dashboard (§2/§4/§6 do that).
accessibility.focus: The active chapter's h2 (tabIndex=-1) receives a visible :focus-visible outline and is the focus-restoration target after a client-side chapter change (verified live in-browser and by ChapterFocusManager.test.tsx).
accessibility.headings: Each ObservatoryShell instance renders exactly one h1 (verified by test). Still not present on the live /share, /, or /dashboard routes until §2/§4/§6 wire the shell in.
accessibility.reduced_motion: Implemented as pure CSS (@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)), not JS-driven — verified structurally by observatory-fallback.test.ts, which asserts the reduced-motion query and the forced-no-3D test hook stay wired to the same classes and both disable the entry animation and 3D transform.
accessibility.critic_mobile_check: True 390x844 and 320x844 layouts fit without horizontal overflow; click navigation and browser back/forward restored focus to the active h2; mobile chapter links were 44px tall.
accessibility.contrast: FAIL: .freshnessLabel computed to rgb(114,109,99) over rgb(11,11,14), 3.82:1 at 12.8px/400.
known_issues: The shell is proven at /dev/observatory-shell only; production routes still lack it until later sections wire it in.
The selected static concentric fallback is not represented; the fallback is a rectangular vertical list.

privacy.logged_out_check: Both new routes render the sign-in form with zero authentication cookie present (curl, no cookie jar).
privacy.public_dollar_leak_check: No $<digits>.<digits> pattern found in either route's unauthenticated HTML — the shell holds no portfolio data of its own by construction.
privacy.shell_cross_render_check: ObservatoryShell.test.tsx asserts the owner slot is never rendered in mode="public", even when one is passed — defensive, not just absence-of-data.
privacy.local_auth_method: Temporary localhost-only OWNER_PASSWORD process override for live screenshot capture; no environment-file contents were read.

failures.criterion: required measured and dimensionally accurate technical-spike evidence
failures.evidence: The decision omits measured load time, long tasks, frame stability, memory, and phone interaction latency. Files labeled 1440x900 are 892x779 or 991x865; committed mobile files are 614x667.
failures.impact: The CSS-versus-R3F decision and visual acceptance cannot be reproduced against the required protocol and target viewports.
failures.required_change: Recreate both spikes long enough to record every required runtime metric and genuine 1440x900/390x844 evidence, verify dimensions, then remove R3F code/dependencies before commit.
failures.verification: Record the measurement protocol and values; run sips over every indexed screenshot; re-run tests/build after cleanup.

failures.verification: Add private, no3d, ordinary public, click, and back/forward URL/focus tests.
